An unidentified presence called the Guest Beyond the Last Door. Warlock 1

Skin, Scales, Fur, or Other Coloration:
Deep forest-green skin with darker green at the knuckles, elbows, and ears.

Hair, Crest, Horns, or Other Distinguishing Features:
Coarse black hair arranged in several thick braids; pronounced lower tusks;
broad nose; one split in the left ear.

Eyes: Yellow-gold

General Appearance:
A strikingly beautiful Orc woman with a heavy jaw, prominent tusks, expressive
yellow-gold eyes, and a direct, memorable face. She does not believe that she
is beautiful and becomes dismissive or uncomfortable when anyone suggests it.

Her body is broad and noticeably overweight without being extreme. Because of
her size, height, and Orcish appearance, strangers often assume that she must
be immensely strong. In fact, she has spent most of her life reading, copying,
administering stores, and performing ritual work. Her Strength 8 is genuine,
and physical effort tires or embarrasses her more quickly than people expect.

She wears a dark blue-gray acolyte robe over fitted leather armor. Her orb is
smoky green glass held in a bronze cage. Her conjured Book of Shadows appears
bound in dark leather with pale stitching and a blank circle stamped into the
cover.

FEATURES AND ABILITIES

Class Features:

Eldritch Invocations
Warlock 1 has selected Pact of the Tome.

Pact of the Tome
At the end of a Short or Long Rest, Warlock 1 can conjure a Book of Shadows.
The book contains three selected cantrips and two selected level-1 Ritual spells.
While the book is on her person, those five selected spells are prepared and
function as Warlock spells for her. Warlock 1 can use the book as a spellcasting
focus.

Pact Magic
Warlock 1 casts Warlock spells using Charisma. Her spell save DC is 13 and
her spell attack bonus is +5. She has one level-1 Pact Magic slot, which
returns after a Short or Long Rest.


Subclass Features:

None at level 1. Warlock subclass is chosen at level 3.

As a Bonus Action, Warlock 1 can Dash and gain 2 Temporary Hit Points. She has
two uses and regains all expended uses after a Short or Long Rest.

Relentless Endurance
Once per Long Rest, when Warlock 1 would be reduced to 0 Hit Points but not
killed outright, she can drop to 1 Hit Point instead.

Warlock 1 knows Guidance and Resistance and always has Inflict Wounds prepared.
Charisma is the spellcasting ability for these spells. Inflict Wounds can be
cast once without a spell slot per Long Rest and can also be cast using the
Pact Magic slot.

Origin Feat: Magic Initiate (Cleric).


PERSONALITY TRAITS

Warlock 1 is strikingly beautiful and almost painfully unaware of it. She does
not merely avoid discussing her appearance. She genuinely believes that other
people are exaggerating, joking, flattering her, or confusing her with someone
else.

Compliments make her insecure and dismissive. She may answer sincere praise
with a suspicious “No, I’m not,” then attempt to change the subject before the
other person can explain.

Warlock 1 sincerely embraces charity and protection, but she also revels in
the destructive side of her magic. A successful Eldritch Blast, Inflict
Wounds, or other violent spell can fill her with exhilaration. She likes the
sensation of power, the visible result, and the knowledge that something
dangerous has been broken because she chose to break it.

That pleasure frightens her afterward. She worries that somewhere inside her
is an evil version of herself who would stop protecting people and begin
seeking destruction for its own sake.

She is physically much weaker than her size suggests. People often look at her
broad Orcish frame and assume that she can lift a wagon. She cannot. She finds
the assumption irritating and faintly humiliating.

IDEALS

Charity.

Warlock 1 believes that people in need should be helped even when the cost is
real and no reward is expected. Shelter, food, healing, and safe passage are
not luxuries to be reserved for people who have proved themselves worthy.

This ideal comes from the Common Table and remains sincere despite the event
that gave her Warlock magic.

Source Roll: Acolyte Ideal d6 result 2.

BONDS

The sanctuary is more than a building. It is a storehouse, kitchen, guest hall,
copying room, and network hub connecting isolated refuges across the wilderness.

Source Roll: Acolyte Bond d6 result 5.

FLAWS

Warlock 1's piety sometimes leads her to trust people who loudly profess faith
or moral purpose.

She is not automatically credulous in every area of life. Her weakness appears
when someone speaks the language of charity, hospitality, pilgrimage, or sacred
duty. She wants such claims to be true and can overlook warning signs that she
would recognize in another context.

That flaw helped the false pilgrims enter the House of Shared Bread.

Source Roll: Acolyte Flaw d6 result 3.

ALLIES AND ORGANIZATIONS

Name or Group: The Common Table
Relationship or Connection:
Warlock 1's religious tradition.

Notes:
The Common Table operates kitchens, shrines, wayhouses, guest halls, and small
refuges. Its teaching emphasizes hospitality, mutual obligation, safe passage,
and the recording of names so that displaced people are not erased.

Supporting Organization Roll: d20 result 5.

Name or Group: The House of Shared Bread
Relationship or Connection:
Warlock 1's former sanctuary and the institution protected by her Bond.

Notes:
The House stands on an isolated road through the wilderness. It offers meals,
sleeping space, letters, route information, and introductions to smaller
refuges.

A stolen Wayfarer Ledger once connected the sanctuary to the hidden locations
of people fleeing coercive institutions. Recovering or neutralizing that
ledger is urgent.

Name or Group: Mother Orra Vale
Relationship or Connection:
Senior keeper of the House of Shared Bread and Warlock 1's first religious
mentor.

Notes:
Orra taught that hospitality is not the absence of caution. A door can remain
open while the people inside still ask who is arriving, what they need, and
whether anyone is following them.

Orra was injured during the attack on the sanctuary. She survived, but her
current health and location are uncertain.

Supporting Relationship Roll: d20 result 1.

Name or Group: The Guest Beyond the Last Door
Relationship or Connection:
Unidentified source associated with Warlock 1's Book of Shadows.

Notes:
The presence first answered during the attack on the House of Shared Bread.
It spoke from blank pages after Warlock 1 prayed for the power to protect the
people inside.

It has not clearly demanded worship, service, or secrecy. That absence of
obvious terms makes the relationship less reassuring rather than more.

CHARACTER NOTES, GOALS, FEARS, AND RELATIONSHIPS

Goals:

Warlock 1 wants to recover the stolen Wayfarer Ledger before its list of
refuges, guides, and displaced travelers can be used to locate vulnerable
people.

She also wants to restore the House of Shared Bread and reconnect the smaller
wayhouses that stopped communicating after the attack.

Her larger goal is to build a safer system in which no single ledger, shrine,
keeper, or captured courier can expose the entire refuge network.

Supporting Goal Roll: d20 result 14.

Fears:

Warlock 1 fears that the presence answering her prayers was not part of the
Common Table at all.

She worries that the Guest Beyond the Last Door learned the language of her
faith, waited until she was frightened enough to accept help without questions,
and entered her life through the Book of Shadows.

She also fears that one of the false pilgrims reached a refuge named in the
Wayfarer Ledger because she personally argued that the strangers should be
admitted.

A second fear is more intimate: she enjoys destructive magic. The exhilaration
is real, and she worries that repeated use will strip away her hesitation until
she becomes an evil version of herself who embraces harm rather than merely
using it.

Supporting Fear Roll: d20 result 4.

Habits or Mannerisms:

She reflexively rejects compliments about her appearance and may become more
insistent the more sincerely they are offered.

Immediately after using destructive magic, she sometimes smiles, laughs, or
stares at the result with open satisfaction. A moment later she becomes
self-conscious and tries to conceal how much she enjoyed it.

She has an intense aversion to small woodland animals and vermin. Squirrels,
chipmunks, hedgehogs, mice, rats, and rabbits all strike her as fundamentally
wrong. She may recoil, climb onto furniture, demand that someone remove the
animal, or repeat “Get her away” with increasing urgency.

This reaction is not based on danger, disease, or a specific traumatic event.
The creatures simply produce an immediate, irrational alarm response.

When asked to lift, drag, or carry something that appears easy for a woman of
her size, she often attempts it once, fails, and becomes defensive before
anyone has commented.

Important Relationships:

Mother Orra Vale:
Religious mentor, injured sanctuary keeper, and the person whose teaching now
complicates Warlock 1's guilt.

The House of Shared Bread:
Her spiritual home and the institution she is determined to protect.

The Guest Beyond the Last Door:
The unknown presence associated with her powers and Book of Shadows.

Other Character Notes:

Warlock 1's patron subclass has not yet been selected. The Guest Beyond the
Last Door is a narrative mystery and does not predetermine a future subclass.

Her Charisma 17 expresses itself through striking presence and beauty rather
than self-confidence. She does not understand the effect she has on other
people and often assumes their reactions must have another cause.

Her silver bell without a clapper came from the House of Shared Bread. Raiders
removed the clapper to prevent it from sounding an alarm. She recovered the
bell after the attack and carries it as a mundane reminder.

Her pleasure in destructive magic does not change her alignment by itself.
It is a source of temptation, fear, and possible character development.

Her aversion to small animals is mechanically severe enough to impose the
Frightened condition as described under Small-Animal Aversion.

Her Book of Shadows disappears and can be reconjured under Pact of the Tome.
The devotional and sanctuary books in her backpack are ordinary physical books.

The Wayfarer Ledger, Mother Orra's fate, the false pilgrims, and the identity
of the Guest Beyond the Last Door are future AI Game Master story hooks.


BACKSTORY

Warlock 1 was raised among Orc families who maintained a rough network of
roads, bridges, seasonal shelters, and supply caches through a sparsely settled
region of the wilderness.

She entered the Common Table as an adolescent and was eventually assigned to
the House of Shared Bread, a sanctuary built where several difficult routes
met.

The House was not a grand temple. It contained a kitchen, storeroom, guest
hall, copying table, shrine alcove, and enough sleeping space for travelers
who could not safely continue after dark.

Warlock 1 copied prayers and letters, recorded arrivals, inspected stored food,
prepared guest spaces, and helped maintain the Wayfarer Ledger. The ledger
connected travelers to guides, refuges, healers, and discreet routes through
the wilderness.

Another acolyte served at the same sanctuary, preserving names and journeys
through spoken recitation, song, and public teaching. Warlock 1 maintained
written records, ritual texts, and stores. Their skills overlapped without
being identical.

A group of travelers arrived during poor weather carrying the symbols and
phrases of a distant charitable order. Warlock 1 argued that the House should
admit them.

The visitors were not pilgrims.

They searched the sanctuary for the Wayfarer Ledger and attacked when Mother
Orra attempted to close the archive room. The raiders removed the clapper from
the sanctuary bell, wounded Orra, and blocked the main exit.

Warlock 1 retreated into the copying room with several guests. She prayed over
an unfinished ledger and asked for the power to protect everyone still inside.

Words appeared on pages that had been blank.

The voice identified itself only as a guest waiting beyond the last door. A
dark Book of Shadows formed in Warlock 1's hands. The magic it contained helped
her force a route through the raiders and move surviving guests out of the
building.

The sanctuary survived, but the Wayfarer Ledger was stolen. Warlock 1 left to
follow the raiders and still serves the Common Table while carrying power that
may have nothing to do with it.


OPTIONAL BACKSTORY

This is optional story material only. It does not establish current party membership, leadership, or party role.

Warlock 1 and Bard 1 served together at the House of Shared Bread. After the sanctuary was attacked and the Wayfarer Ledger stolen, they left together to follow the raiders. Their investigation led toward an illegal trapping and labor camp where names from the sanctuary network were being used to identify fugitives and vulnerable travelers. Druid 1 had independently tracked injured animals, damaged land, and unusual traffic to the same place. Barbarian 1 entered by another route seeking contracts, keys, and payroll records. The four investigations collided inside the camp. Druid 1 found a safe route through the surrounding wilds, Barbarian 1 opened a barred service gate, and Warlock 1 and Bard 1 used magic, ritual knowledge, and coordination to move captives through the confusion. The four escaped together and continued traveling as the Wild party.

These are setting-neutral narrative institutions and story hooks. They grant

Source or Rules Reference:

Rule, Feature, Item, or Spell:
Small-Animal Aversion

Full Effect:
Warlock 1 has an intense irrational fear of living squirrels, chipmunks,
hedgehogs, mice, rats, rabbits, and similar small creatures.

When she can see one of these creatures within 30 feet, she automatically has
the Frightened condition. The visible creature is the source of the fear. No
saving throw is made.

The condition ends immediately when no qualifying creature is visible within
30 feet. It can begin again whenever one becomes visible within that range.

While Frightened in this way, Warlock 1 follows the normal rules for the
Frightened condition. She has Disadvantage on ability checks and attack rolls
while the source of fear is within line of sight, and she cannot willingly
move closer to it.

Ordinary pictures, carvings, toys, tracks, and mentions of such creatures do
not trigger the condition. The AI Game Master may treat a swarm as a
qualifying source if it is visibly composed of one of the listed creatures.

Source or Rules Reference:
WardensPC character-specific homebrew; normal Frightened condition rules.

feats_and_features: Eldritch Invocations: Pact of the Tome. SRD rules: You have unearthed Eldritch Invocations, pieces of forbidden knowledge that imbue you with an abiding magical ability or other lessons. You gain one invocation of your choice, such as Pact of the Tome. Invocations are described in the “Eldritch Invocation Options” section later in this class’s description. Prerequisites. If an invocation has a prerequisite, you must meet it to learn that invocation. For example, if an invocation requires you to be a level 5+ Warlock, you can select the invocation once you reach Warlock level 5. Replacing and Gaining Invocations. Whenever you gain a Warlock level, you can replace one of your invocations with another one for which you qualify. You can’t replace an invocation if it’s a prerequisite for another invocation that you have. When you gain certain Warlock levels, you gain more invocations of your choice, as shown in the Invocations column of the Warlock Features table. You can’t pick the same invocation more than once unless its description says otherwise.

Pact of the Tome: can conjure Book of Shadows at the end of a Short or Long Rest; book supplies selected cantrips and selected level-1 ritual spells as prepared Warlock spells while on her person, and functions as a focus. SRD rules: Stitching together strands of shadow, you conjure forth a book in your hand at the end of a Short or Long Rest. This Book of Shadows (you determine its appearance) contains eldritch magic that only you can access, granting you the benefits below. The book disappears if you conjure another book with this feature or if you die. Cantrips and Rituals. When the book appears, choose three cantrips, and choose two level 1 spells that have the Ritual tag. The spells can be from any class’s spell list, and they must be spells you don’t already have prepared. While the book is on your person, you have the chosen spells prepared, and they function as Warlock spells for you. Spellcasting Focus. You can use the book as a Spellcasting Focus.

Pact Magic: Charisma casting; one level-1 Pact Magic slot recovered on a Short or Long Rest. SRD rules: Through occult ceremony, you have formed a pact with a mysterious entity to gain magical powers. The entity is a voice in the shadows—its identity unclear—but its boon to you is concrete: the ability to cast spells. See “Spells” for the rules on spellcasting. The information below details how you use those rules with Warlock spells, which appear in the Warlock spell list later in the class’s description. Cantrips. You know two Warlock cantrips of your choice. Eldritch Blast and Prestidigitation are recommended. Whenever you gain a Warlock level, you can replace one of your cantrips from this feature with another Warlock cantrip of your choice. When you reach Warlock levels 4 and 10, you learn another Warlock cantrip of your choice, as shown in the Cantrips column of the Warlock Features table. Spell Slots. The Warlock Features table shows how many spell slots you have to cast your Warlock spells of levels 1–5. The table also shows the level of those slots, all of which are the same level. You regain all expended Pact Magic spell slots when you finish a Short or Long Rest. For example, when you’re a level 5 Warlock, you have two level 3 spell slots. To cast the level 1 spell Charm Person, you must spend one of those slots, and you cast it as a level 3 spell. Prepared Spells of Level 1+. You prepare the list of level 1+ spells that are available for you to cast with this feature. To start, choose two level 1 Warlock spells. Charm Person and Hex are recommended. The number of spells on your list increases as you gain Warlock levels, as shown in the Prepared Spells column of the Warlock Features table. Whenever that number increases, choose additional Warlock spells until the number of spells on your list matches the number in the table. The chosen spells must be of a level no higher than what’s shown in the table’s Slot Level column for your level. When you reach level 6, for example, you learn a new Warlock spell, which can be of levels 1–3. If another Warlock feature gives you spells that you always have prepared, those spells don’t count
Orc: Humanoid, Medium, 30-foot Speed, Darkvision 120 feet.

Adrenaline Rush: Bonus Action Dash and gain 2 Temporary Hit Points; 2 uses per Short or Long Rest. SRD rules: You can take the Dash action as a Bonus Action. When you do so, you gain a number of Temporary Hit Points equal to your Proficiency

Relentless Endurance: once per Long Rest, drop to 1 HP instead of 0 when not killed outright. SRD rules: When you are reduced to 0 Hit Points but not killed outright, you can drop to 1 Hit Point instead. Once you use this trait, you can’t do so again until you finish a Long Rest.

Magic Initiate (Cleric): Guidance, Resistance, and always-prepared Inflict Wounds using Charisma; one free Long Rest casting, with Pact Magic casting also allowed. SRD rules: Origin Feat. You gain the following benefits. Two Cantrips. You learn two cantrips of your choice from the Cleric, Druid, or Wizard spell list. Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is your spellcasting ability for this feat’s spells (choose when you select this feat). Level 1 Spell. Choose a level 1 spell from the same list you selected for this feat’s cantrips. You always have that spell prepared. You can cast it once without a spell slot, and you regain the ability to cast it in that way when you finish a Long Rest. You can also cast the spell using any spell slots you have. Spell Change. Whenever you gain a new level, you can replace one of the spells you chose for this feat with a different spell of the same level from the chosen spell list. Repeatable. You can take this feat more than once, but you must choose a different spell list each time.
